predecessors.name: Czechoslovakia
predecessors.text: Slovakia, which 'voted to secede from Czecho-Slovakia' on 14 March 1939

successors.name: Czechoslovakia
successors.text: 'its territory was reintegrated into the recreated Third Czechoslovak Republic'; the strip lost to Hungary in 1939 came back with it

ledger.x: 14 March 1939: the Slovak Diet declares an independent Slovak State, a client of Nazi Germany.
23 March 1939: the Treaty of Protection makes the new state a German client.
4 April 1939: the war ends in the Budapest treaty.
4 April 1939: Slovakia cedes the Stakčín–Sobrance strip to Hungary.
21 November 1939: Germany hands Slovakia Orava and Spiš, taken from Poland.
29 August 1944: the Slovak National Uprising begins at Banská Bystrica against the Tiso government and the German troops.
19 January 1945: the Red Army enters eastern Slovakia.
April 1945: the Red Army drives the Germans out.
4 April 1945: Bratislava falls to the 2nd Ukrainian Front in the Bratislava–Brno offensive and the Red Army 'occupied all of Slovakia'; the fighting on Slovak soil ends with the state.
4 April 1945: the client state ends with the fall of Bratislava (infobox 'Fall of Bratislava: 4 April 1945'); the exiled government capitulated on 8 May 1945.
4 April 1945: the Slovak Republic ends with the fall of Bratislava; its territory 'was reintegrated into the recreated Third Czechoslovak Republic'.

wars.name: Slovak–Hungarian War
wars.outcome: Hungary wins a strip of eastern Slovakia (1,697 km2) by the Budapest treaty of 4 April 1939; a ceasefire came about 25 March and fighting stopped 31 March.

wars.name: Invasion of Poland
wars.outcome: Slovakia took part with Germany in September 1939 and was awarded Orava and Spiš by the German–Slovak agreement of 21 November 1939.

wars.name: Slovak National Uprising
wars.outcome: The German troops and Slovak loyalists crush the organised uprising: Banská Bystrica falls 27 October and Viest's last order is given 28 October 1944; insurgent territory fell from about 22,000 km2 to under 7,000 km2.

wars.name: Western Carpathian offensive
wars.outcome: The Red Army takes eastern Slovakia from 19 January 1945 (Prešov the same day); the Western Carpathian offensive 'lasted from January 12 to February 18, 1945', the 2nd Ukrainian Front reached the Hron by mid-March and took Bratislava on 4 April 1945, ending…

certainty.note: Borders follow treaties: the 2 November 1938 Vienna Award line, the 4 April 1939 Budapest treaty and the 21 November 1939 German–Slovak agreement.
